clue.text: Communication from detective's sphere of operations

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector, so 'detective's' gives DI's, written DIS
a patch is an area someone works or is responsible for, like a police officer's beat

explanation.surface: A message comes in from the area a police detective covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sphere of operations' sounds like part of the definition but is the PATCH, the beat a detective works.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official message or report sent from one place to another.

indicators.note: endless says the word for attraction loses its final letter

parts.note: charm is the power to attract or delight

explanation.surface: Some animal living in a lake has a pull that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter, M, from CHARM.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a fish of the trout family found in cold, deep lakes.

definitions.meaning: to free means to buy back or release, as a captive or a pawned item
to cash means to exchange a voucher or bond for money

explanation.surface: Free money on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeeming means both rescuing someone from bondage and converting coupons or bonds into money.

indicators.note: but not says a letter is to be dropped from the word for set

parts.note: a set of people or things is a group

explanation.surface: A musical scale is fixed, though not correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like the musical kind but means to climb; GROUP loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to climb it, ascend.

clue.text: Reckoning advanced pupil will get further

parts.note: reckoning, working out a sum, is addition
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
L stands for learner, the pupil driver's plate

explanation.surface: A sum done by a bright student will get them further on.
explanation.definitionFit: Further and additional are synonyms meaning extra, more.

indicators.note: initially removed says the first letter of the word for barrier is taken away

parts.note: a railing is a fence or barrier of rails

explanation.surface: A rickety fence was taken down at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially removed' drops the R from RAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ailing is sick or in poor health, so not sound.

parts.note: a view as a noun is a sight
to view, as a verb, is to see

explanation.surface: A tour seen from two different angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' is taken once as a noun (SIGHT) and once as a verb (SEE); the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to visit and look round places of interest, as on a sightseeing tour.

indicators.note: out says the points sit outside the word for pale

parts.note: S and S are two compass points, south twice
wan means pale
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone indicates some pale blue material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts the two points SS outside WAN; 'blue' looks like a colour beside 'pale' but means DOWN, low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansdown is a soft thick fabric, so it is a stuff in the old sense of woven material.

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the name are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Dorian is distressed by an official decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DORIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or decree officially.

indicators.note: hidden in says the letter for kilo goes inside the word for the soldier

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
K is the abbreviation for kilo and its NATO alphabet letter

explanation.surface: A kilogram of something is stashed in a soldier's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' puts K inside PARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: Ten page extract set out — it's quite clear

indicators.note: set out says the word for extract is spread open around the other letters

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out or extract
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An excerpt of ten pages is laid out and is easy to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract' reads as a noun, a passage, but is a verb, ELICIT; 'set out' puts XP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly, leaving nothing in doubt.

clue.text: Cause trouble, being found with object

parts.note: to found a business is to start it
an object is a something, a thing

explanation.surface: Someone causes a row by being caught with a certain object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past tense of find but is to found, to start.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is an idiom for provoking a fight or argument.

clue.text: Developing food range-that's about right in area of high growth

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the letter for right
developing says the letters of food and range are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A new food range is promoted in a fast-growing area of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developing' rearranges FOOD RANGE and 'about' wraps that round R; 'high growth' sounds like economics but means plants grown up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof garden is a garden on a building's roof, where plants grow high above the street.

clue.text: Make impression when deal goes ahead

indicators.note: goes ahead says the word for deal comes first, in front of the other piece

parts.note: to deal is to trade
a mark is an impression left on something

explanation.surface: Someone makes an impression when a business deal is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like a verb but is a noun, a brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A make of car or clothing is a brand, identified by its registered name or logo.

parts.note: a hoop is a circular band
O is round in shape
E, east, is one of the four cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: A ring encircles a red-plumaged cardinal bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like the bird or churchman but is a cardinal point, E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with a long curved bill found in Europe, Asia and Africa.

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the old charmer's word takes a letter inside

parts.note: a magus is an ancient sorcerer or wise man; the 's is 'has'
N is an abbreviation for Norse

explanation.surface: An ancient magician hosts a Scandinavian holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norse saint' reads as one phrase, but 'Norse' only gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: St Magnus was an earl of Orkney revered as a saint and martyr.

parts.note: dotty usually means mad, but here it means made of dots, done with an artist's technique

explanation.surface: Someone is a little mad in an arty way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippled work is painted or drawn with many small dots instead of lines.

clue.text: Insist engine he is sold has broken down

indicators.note: broken down says the letters of those words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A dealer insists that the engine he sold has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' rearranges ENGINE HE IS SOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig one's heels in is an idiom for refusing to budge, standing firm.

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word for count reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a poll is a count of votes or heads

explanation.surface: A party helps count votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns POLL into LLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a serving or spoonful of food, a helping.

clue.text: Athletic type accepting a little money by the end of the day

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for type holds the coin inside

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
P stands for a penny, a small sum

indicators.note: the end of picks the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A sporty person takes some cash by nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athletic type' reads as one phrase, but 'type' is SORT, with P inside and Y from the end of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty is fond of games and physically fit.

parts.note: a fresco is a painting done on wet plaster

explanation.surface: An American left a mural in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Done al fresco means held in the open air, outdoors.

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word for support is said out loud

parts.note: to shore up a wall is to support it with props

explanation.surface: Someone voiced backing for a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SHORE and SHAW are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright, author of Pygmalion.

parts.note: fabulous usually means wonderful, but here it means writing fables, by an ancient Greek author

explanation.surface: A brilliant ancient author.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of moral animal fables.

clue.text: Business that's part of stylish operation

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A firm is a component of a slick enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included "that's", which is the link word joining definition and wordplay, so the definition is just 'Business'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop is a retail business, a store.

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted round, says the letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman, someone with an injury from the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind; it rearranges ONE and WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a female first name, as in the Saxon heroine of Scott's Ivanhoe.

clue.text: Accept deliveries, showing assumption of control

parts.note: to accept is to take
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled by one bowler

explanation.surface: Receiving parcels shows someone is taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests parcels but is cricket: an over is six balls bowled in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeover is when a person or company seizes control of a business.
